answer: For a poll on a jade sculpture by the river ridge, the server assigns every ballot weight 1 divided by the size of its account's closed neighborhood in a frozen mutual-link graph. It rejects ballots from accounts absent from the graph. In an isolated clique of k voting accounts, each ballot has weight 1/k, so their total weight is one. Gaining weight by splitting that clique requires removing links, potentially sacrificing their benefits. Unlinked fake accounts retain full weight, while genuine neighbors are discounted.
